timeline.title: The Lullabies Sung Before You
items: One of the first books of nursery rhymes, Mother Goose's Melody, was printed in London for little ones.
Jane Taylor published a poem called The Star. We still sing it to babies all over the world.
Sarah Josepha Hale wrote the rhyme about a lamb who followed Mary to school one day.
Johannes Brahms published his Wiegenlied, the gentle cradle song still hummed at bedtime.
today: A brand new song begins. And we will sing it to you for the rest of our lives.

letters.title: What the World Has Said About Babies
items: Every child begins the world again.
A baby is God's opinion that the world should go on.
Every child comes with the message that God is not yet discouraged of man.
It takes a village to raise a child.
letters.hand: Our village is ready, {first}. And it already adores you.

facts.title: The Clever Science of Being New
items: From the very start, newborns love looking at faces more than almost anything else.
Newborns already know the voices they heard most often before they were born.
New babies see best at about the distance from a cuddling arm to a loving face.
Real smiles usually arrive at around six to eight weeks. Worth every sleepy night.
Scientists have seen very young babies copy faces, like poking a tongue out back at a grown up.
Tiny babies can hear the sounds of every language, then tune in to their family's own.
facts.hand: You were born clever, {first}. You were also born loved.

world.kicker: A welcome from all of us
world.title: Why the World Is Better With You in It
world.lead: The day you arrived, the world got:
items: A brand new laugh it had never heard.
Someone new to sing to at bedtime.
A whole family who fell in love at once.
A reason for everyone to call home.
A future full of things only you will do.
And the sweetest little person we know.
world.close: The world got better on {born}, {first}. Ours most of all.

promises.title: Our promises to you
items: To sing to you, even badly.
To hold your hand until you let go.
To keep every drawing you ever make.
To cheer for you at everything.
To love you, always, whatever you become.

note.title: What we believe a new baby is
paras: We make magazines for a living, but this one was for someone very new.
We believe a new baby is the start of a thousand stories. The first smile, the first word, the first wobbly step. All of it still ahead, all of it already loved.
{first}, before you could even hold your head up, someone wanted the whole world to know you had arrived. They wanted you to read this one day and know.
That someone is {from}. From everything they told us, you were loved before you were even here.
note.wish: Welcome to the world, {first}. It is so glad you came.
